items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: But for the most part, Yank didn’t like to do that. I mean it was done, it was recorded and it was done, and he just felt there was much more freedom and flexibility in picking a tune

ctx.x: So was the music arranged at all?

A lot of it was arranged, but a lot of it we didn’t use. I mean they arranged it for recording purposes, and sometimes I guess if it was expected, they would put up some arrangements on a concert and we would play them. But for the most part, Yank didn’t like to do that. I mean it was done, it was recorded and it was done, and he just felt there was much more freedom and flexibility in picking a tune and having everybody — you know it was such a nice experience because in ensemble playing, everybody had a certain…
Wow. What about, was it tough financially to keep that kind of size group together at these times? This was what, the mid-70s?
